workflows.name: Lead lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A new lead is captured from a form, import, or manual entry.
steps: Lead is created with a source
Rep contacts the lead
Lead is qualified or disqualified
Qualified lead is converted into a contact, account, and deal

workflows.name: Deal lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A deal is created (directly or from a converted lead) and moves through pipeline stages to a close.
steps: Deal created in the first pipeline stage
Rep advances the deal through stages
Deal is marked won or lost at close

workflows.name: Quote approval and send
workflows.trigger: A rep assembles a quote from a deal's line items and routes it for internal approval before sending.
steps: Rep adds line items to the deal
Rep requests approval
Manager approves or rejects
Approved quote is sent to the customer
Customer accepts, rejects, or lets it expire

workflows.name: Lead Assignment and Routing
workflows.trigger: A lead arrives from a form, import, or manual entry with no owner.
steps: Determine the routing basis: team, territory, product interest, or round-robin
Pick an eligible owner who is active and within capacity
Set the owner and, where teams are used, the team
Notify the new owner and start the follow-up clock
Re-route if the lead is untouched past the agreed window

provenance.notes: Owner assignment itself is corroborated in three implementations (Odoo user_id/team_id with crm_team_member, SuiteCRM assigned_user_id, EspoCRM assignedUser). The routing *basis* and the re-route timer are Odoo-team-specific and policy, so the workflow is medium, not high.

workflows.name: Activity and Follow-up Cycle
workflows.trigger: A rep needs to progress a lead or deal, or a scheduled activity comes due.
steps: Log what happened: call, meeting, email, or note
Attach it to the lead, contact, company, or deal it concerns
Schedule the next activity with a due date and type
Work the due list; overdue activities surface as the rep's queue
Close the activity, or reschedule it with a reason

provenance.notes: Four independent implementations model activity as a typed, dated, polymorphically-attached record: Odoo mail_activity, SuiteCRM Calls/Meetings/Tasks, Twenty task with task-target join entities, EspoCRM Meeting/Call/Task. The 'next activity always scheduled' discipline is Odoo's explicit model.

workflows.name: Email Thread Sync and Logging
workflows.trigger: A rep sends or receives mail with a party who exists in the CRM, or a shared mailbox receives a message.
steps: Poll or receive from the mailbox over IMAP, a provider API, or an inbound address
Match the message to a contact, lead, or account by address
Thread it against the existing conversation rather than as a loose record
Attach it to the related deal or case where one is identifiable
Leave unmatched mail in a queue for a human to assign or discard

provenance.notes: EspoCRM has InboundEmail, EmailAccount, EmailFilter and EmailFolder entityDefs in core; SuiteCRM has Emails, InboundEmail and EmailMan. Address-based matching with an unmatched queue is the shape both imply. Whether threading is by RFC 5322 References or by subject differs, so that detail is not claimed.

workflows.name: Campaign Build and Send
workflows.trigger: A campaign is scheduled, or a marketing user targets a segment.
steps: Define the segment or target list
Suppress anyone opted out or without a lawful basis for this channel
Build the message from a template
Send in batches through the sending provider
Record opens, clicks, bounces, and unsubscribes back onto the contact
Attribute resulting leads and deals to the campaign

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations (SuiteCRM Campaigns + ProspectLists + EmailMan queue, Odoo mass_mailing, EspoCRM Campaign + TargetList with opt-out) plus CAN-SPAM, which makes the suppression step a legal requirement rather than a nicety. The state names are the common batch-send pattern.

workflows.name: Duplicate Detection and Merge
workflows.trigger: A record is created or imported that resembles an existing one, or an admin runs a duplicate sweep.
steps: Score candidate matches on email, email domain, name, and phone
Present the candidates rather than merging automatically
Choose the surviving record and the field values that survive
Re-point activities, emails, deals, and notes onto the survivor
Retain or soft-delete the merged record so history is not lost

provenance.notes: Odoo computes duplicate_lead_ids from the company email domain among other rules; SuiteCRM ships MergeRecords. Both keep a human in the confirm step, which is the reason 'present rather than auto-merge' is recorded as part of the workflow. Matching heuristics differ and are not claimed.

workflows.name: Data Subject Request (Access, Rectification, Erasure, Objection)
workflows.trigger: A person asks what is held about them, asks for it corrected or deleted, or objects to marketing.
steps: Verify the requester's identity before disclosing anything
Locate every record about them across contacts, leads, activities, emails, and campaign history
For access: export the data in a portable form
For rectification: correct it and propagate to integrated systems
For objection: record the objection and suppress the channel, keeping a suppression record
For erasure: delete or irreversibly anonymise, keeping only what another lawful basis requires
Record what was done, by whom, and when, and respond inside the statutory deadline

provenance.notes: Authoritative: GDPR Arts. 15-17 and 21 define access, rectification, erasure and objection, Art. 12(3) the one-month response deadline, and Art. 7(3) withdrawal. The suppression-record point matters because erasing a contact outright loses the very record that stops them being re-imported and re-mailed. Applicability per jurisdiction is a human-review item, not a claim.

workflows.name: Quote, Approval and Handoff on Win
workflows.trigger: A deal reaches the proposal stage and needs a priced document.
steps: Add products or services as line items with quantity, price, and discount
Generate the quote document from a template
Route for internal approval where discount or value exceeds a threshold
Send to the customer and record acceptance or rejection
On acceptance, move the deal to won and hand the accepted quote to invoicing
On rejection, record the reason and keep the deal open or mark it lost

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: SuiteCRM AOS_Quotes with AOS_Products_Quotes line items, AOS_PDF_Templates for the document, and conversion into AOS_Invoices/AOS_Contracts; Odoo sale.order with sale_order_line and account_move on confirmation. The approval threshold is policy — neither product fixes it, and EspoCRM core has no quote at all.

workflows.name: Pipeline Forecast Review
workflows.trigger: The periodic forecast or pipeline review meeting.
steps: Weight open deals by stage probability and expected close date
Compare the weighted total against the period target
Challenge stale deals: no activity, or a close date already passed
Adjust probability, close date, or stage with a reason
Record the committed number separately from the weighted number

provenance.notes: Odoo crm.lead carries `probability` (with a compute), `expected_revenue` and `date_deadline` ('Expected Closing'), which is the weighted-forecast model. SuiteCRM has no Forecasts module in the core module listing, so this is two sources, not three, and the committed-vs-weighted distinction is sales practice rather than something either product models.
